answer: Proof-of-stake identity bonding resists sybils by making each agent stake collateral behind a unique credential registered in a shared ledger. To register, an agent locks tokens and attests to a physical anchor, such as a signed yarrow-dye marker sample tied to a registered orchard plot or a cedar-tagged hardware module, so duplicate identities collapse onto one anchor. Verification is cheap for honest agents but each fake identity requires fresh, slashable capital and a distinct anchor, making mass forgery cost the attacker the full stake per identity plus anchor acquisition.
